comment: Port map for netlists/rx_pad.cir, the receiver's input pad network.
z0 pad = 50 ohm: the package side of the ball is a 50 ohm
single-ended, 100 ohm differential environment, and the deck's own
RT1/RT2 terminate it to the same number, so the match is good at
low frequency and degrades with the pad capacitance.
z0 gate = 750 ohm, AND THIS IS A CHOICE WITH A LIMIT. The load this
network actually drives is the CTLE's gate, which is a capacitance:
26.7 fF, computed in ctle_rx.cir's header. A port reference is a
REAL impedance, so no number can equal a capacitive load at every
frequency, and anyone reading these S-parameters should know that
before they use them.
750 ohm is the magnitude of that gate impedance at 7.80 GHz:
7.80 GHz is where the CTLE this network feeds peaks, so the
reference is right at the one frequency the output is bought for,
and progressively wrong away from it -- too low below (the real
gate is a higher impedance there, so the measurement loads the node
more than the CTLE does) and too high above.
The alternative considered and rejected: put the 26.7 fF in the
deck and make the gate ports nearly transparent with a very high
reference. That would fold the load into the network under test, so
the published S-parameters would no longer be the pad network's --
they would be the pad network plus one particular load, and could
not be cascaded with any other.
bias natural on a deck with no DC sources: there is no operating
point to measure and every port resolves to 0 V, which is correct.
A passive R-C network has the same small-signal behaviour at every
bias.
passive_comment: Resistors and capacitors only: no transistor card, no controlled
source, no gyrator. So the passivity and reciprocity checks apply,
and they are not expected to be close calls --
passivity:   largest singular value of S must be <= 1, and
strictly below it wherever the two 50 ohm
terminations and the 8 ohm route carry current;
reciprocity: S21 and S12 must be equal to the simulator's
numerical floor, not to a tolerance.
Both are run on the transistor-side 4-port AND on the model's own
measured SDD21/SDD12, because a model that passed the first and
failed the second would be a model that invented gain.
bands_comment: PROPOSED, and not yet read by the tool (step 3a). This network has
no zero and no peaking: it is a low-pass whose only corner is the
pad capacitance. Two bands, for the flat part and the part where the

bands.name: flat
reason: Below 2 GHz the pad capacitance is a small perturbation: 125 fF
differential has a reactance of 637 ohm at 2 GHz against the
100 ohm reference, so the network is essentially its resistors.

bands.name: pad_dominated
reason: From 2 GHz the pad capacitance sets the response. Its reactance
crosses the 100 ohm differential reference at 12.7 GHz, inside
this band, which is why the match degrades through it.

bands.name: below_step_ceiling
reason: To be FIXED as a number from the first measured run: the
model's own ten-steps-per-period ceiling, written down once and
then never re-derived from the model under test.

bars_comment: Empty on purpose: report-only until the per-band numbers are
measured and the bars are approved (step 5).
